description: Laravel-style model factories for Prisma: tests and seeds declare the records they need through a fluent, fully typed API, inferred from the generated Prisma client. No codegen, no schema parsing, no build step.
rules: Import from "@flefebvre/prisma-factorio". ESM only, Node >= 20; there is no CommonJS require entry. `@prisma/client` >=7 <8 is the only required peer.
Bootstrap once per client: `const prismaFactorio = initPrismaFactorio(() => prisma, { seed, locale })`. Prefer the thunk — it is called on the first create() and never again.
The library never builds a Prisma client; the caller passes their own. A Prisma 7 client is constructed with a driver adapter.
Every fluent call returns a new factory. `userFactory.count(3)` leaves userFactory untouched, so factories are safe to share, compose and export from a module.
create() persists through the client and returns the real database row — or an array of rows when the factory carries count(n).
Definitions are checked against the model's Prisma create input, nested relation input included. A misspelled field or a state that does not exist is a compile error, not a runtime surprise.
States declared in the config become typed methods on the factory: a `suspended` state gives `userFactory.suspended()`. Add one on the chain with .state().

Attach a parent with for(), children with has(), or put a factory or row directly in a relation field of the definition. Prefer for() and has(): a wrong-model row in a relation attribute is not type-checked.
The library opens no transaction of its own — atomicity is the caller's. Route a whole graph through one with `prisma.$transaction((tx) => factory.using(tx).create())`.
A definition receives { faker, index, uid } and is evaluated once per record, so count(n) yields n distinct records rather than n copies.
seed pins faker's values and recycle's picks, but does not make a run reproducible: uid draws a fresh random prefix per process, so never snapshot uid-derived columns.
recycle() hands existing rows to a graph so it connects them instead of creating duplicates. A pooled row whose relation is backed by a required foreign key can be connected once only.

afterCreating callbacks run on the completed record, declared in the config or added on the chain. A throwing callback rejects create() and rolls nothing back unless you are inside your own transaction.
There is no code generation of any kind and no generator to add to schema.prisma: every type is inferred from the Prisma client you already generate.

An explicit `id` and a belongs-to relation field cannot be passed together — naming an id forces Prisma's unchecked create input, which drops relation fields. Pass the raw foreign key instead, or let the id be generated.
Records are written one create() at a time, sequentially. There is no createMany fast path, because relations, callbacks and returned rows all depend on created-then-continue semantics.
